relevant_trials.brief_summary: This phase III trial studies cabozantinib to see how well it works compared with placebo in treating patients with neuroendocrine or carcinoid tumors that may have spread from where it first started to nearby tissue, lymph nodes, or distant parts of the body (advanced). Cabozantinib is a chemotherapy drug known as a tyrosine kinase inhibitor, and it targets specific tyrosine kinase receptors, that when blocked, may slow tumor growth.
relevant_trials.detailed_description:
PRIMARY OBJECTIVES:

I. To determine whether cabozantinib (cabozantinib S-malate) can significantly improve progression-free survival (PFS) compared to placebo in patients with advanced pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (NET) whose disease has progressed after prior therapy.

II. To determine whether cabozantinib can significantly improve progression-free survival (PFS) compared to placebo in patients with advanced carcinoid tumors whose disease has progressed after prior therapy.

SECONDARY OBJECTIVES:

I. To determine whether cabozantinib can significantly improve overall survival (OS) compared to placebo in patients with advanced pancreatic NET whose disease has progressed after prior therapy.

II. To determine whether cabozantinib can significantly improve overall survival (OS) compared to placebo in patients with advanced carcinoid tumors whose disease has progressed after prior therapy.

III. To evaluate safety and tolerability of cabozantinib versus placebo in patients with advanced pancreatic NET using Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) and Patient-Reported Outcomes Version of the Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (PRO-CTCAE).

IV. To evaluate safety and tolerability of cabozantinib versus placebo in patients with advanced carcinoid tumors using CTCAE and PRO-CTCAE.

V. To evaluate the overall radiographic response rate of cabozantinib versus placebo in patients with advanced pancreatic NET whose disease has progressed after prior therapy.

VI. To evaluate the overall radiographic response rate of cabozantinib versus placebo in patients with advanced carcinoid tumors whose disease has progressed after prior therapy.

OTHER OBJECTIVE:

I. Results of the primary analysis will be examined for consistency, while taking into account the stratification factors and/or covariates of baseline quality of life (QOL) and fatigue.

QUALITY OF LIFE SUBSTUDY OBJECTIVE:

I. To compare overall quality of life, disease-related symptoms, and other domains between the two treatment groups (cabozantinib versus \[vs.\] placebo) within each cohort of patients (pancreatic NET vs. carcinoid tumor). (Quality of Life Substudy Objective - A021602-HO1)

POPULATION PHARMACOKINETICS SUBSTUDY OBJECTIVE:

I. To describe the population pharmacokinetic and exposure-response relationships of cabozantinib in patients with advanced neuroendocrine tumors. (Population Pharmacokinetics Substudy Objective - A021602-PP1)

OUTLINE: Patients are randomized to 1 of 2 arms.

ARM I: Patients receive cabozantinib S-malate orally (PO) once daily (QD) on days 1-28 of each cycle. Cycles repeat every 28 days in the absence of disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. Patients also undergo blood and urine sample collection, and computed tomography (CT), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and/or x-ray imaging during screening and on study.

ARM II: Patients receive placebo PO QD on days 1-28 of each cycle. Cycles repeat every 28 days in the absence of disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. Patients also undergo blood and urine sample collection, and CT, MRI, and/or x-ray imaging during screening and on study. Patients may crossover to receive cabozantinib S-malate at the time of disease progression.

After completion of study treatment, patients are followed up every 12 weeks until disease progression or start of new anticancer therapy, and then every 6 months until 8 years after registration.
relevant_trials.eligibility_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Documentation of Disease:

  * Histologic Documentation: Well- or moderately-differentiated neuroendocrine tumors of pancreatic and non-pancreatic (i.e. carcinoid) origin by local pathology

    * The pathology report must state ONE of the following: 1) well- or moderately-differentiated neuroendocrine tumor, 2) low- or intermediate-grade neuroendocrine tumor, or 3) carcinoid tumor or atypical carcinoid tumor; documentation of histology from a primary or metastatic site is allowed
    * Patients with poorly differentiated neuroendocrine carcinoma, high-grade neuroendocrine carcinoma without specification of differentiation status, adenocarcinoid tumor, or goblet cell carcinoid tumor are not eligible. Patients with well-differentiated grade 3 neuroendocrine tumor are eligible
  * Stage: Locally advanced/unresectable or metastatic disease
  * Tumor Site: Histological documentation of neuroendocrine tumor of pancreatic, gastrointestinal (GI), lung, thymus, other, or unknown primary site; GI, lung, thymus, other, and unknown primary NETs will enroll in the carcinoid tumor cohort of the study

    * Functional (i.e., associated with symptoms or clinical syndrome related to hormone secretion by tumor) or nonfunctional tumors are allowed
  * Radiologic Evaluation: Target lesions must have shown evidence of disease progression by Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) version (v)1.1 criteria in the 12 months prior to registration; the radiologic images, imaging reports, and clinic notes indicating growth of existing lesions, development of new lesions, or treatment changes must be submitted
* Measurable Disease

  * Patients must have measurable disease per RECIST 1.1 by computer tomography (CT) scan or magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
  * Lesions must be accurately measured in at least one dimension (longest diameter to be recorded) as \>= 1 cm with CT or MRI (or \>= 1.5 cm for lymph nodes); non-measurable disease includes disease smaller than these dimensions or lesions considered truly non-measurable including: leptomeningeal disease, ascites, pleural or pericardial effusion, lymphangitic involvement of skin or lung
* Prior Treatment

  * Patient must have experienced disease progression after receiving or intolerance leading to treatment discontinuation of at least one Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved line of therapy (except somatostatin analogs); prior lines of therapy must include one of the following: everolimus, sunitinib, or lutetium Lu 177 dotatate in patients with pancreatic NET; everolimus in patients with lung NET; everolimus or lutetium Lu 177 dotatate in patients with gastrointestinal NET
  * Prior treatment (except somatostatin analogs) with biologic therapy, immunotherapy, chemotherapy, investigational agent for malignancy, and/or radiation must be completed at least 28 days prior to registration
  * Prior treatment with somatostatin analogs is allowed, and continuation of treatment with somatostatin analogs while on cabozantinib/placebo is allowed provided that the patient has been on a stable dose for at least two months
  * Prior systemic treatment with radionuclide therapy must be completed at least 6 weeks prior to registration
  * Prior treatment with hepatic artery embolization (including bland embolization, chemoembolization, and selective internal radiation therapy) or ablative therapies is allowed if measurable disease remains outside of the treated area or if there is documented disease progression in a treated site; prior liver-directed or other ablative treatment must be completed at least 28 days prior to registration
  * Prior treatment with cabozantinib is not allowed
  * Patients should have resolution of any toxic effects of prior therapy (except alopecia and fatigue) to National Cancer Institute (NCI) CTCAE, version 5.0, grade 1 or less
  * Patients must have completed any major surgery at least 12 weeks prior to registration and any minor surgery (including uncomplicated tooth extractions) at least 28 days prior to registration; complete wound healing from major surgery must have occurred at least 28 days prior to registration, and complete wound healing from minor surgery must have occurred at least 10 days prior to registration
* Patient History

  * No class III or IV congestive heart failure (CHF) within 6 months of registration
  * No clinically significant cardiac arrhythmia within 6 months of registration
  * No unstable angina or myocardial infarction (MI) within 6 months of registration
  * No thromboembolic events within 6 months of registration (including \[incl.\] stroke, transient ischemic attack \[TIA\], deep vein thrombosis \[DVT\], \& pulmonary embolism \[PE\])
  * No known history of congenital long QT syndrome
  * No uncontrolled hypertension within 14 days of registration (defined as systolic blood pressure \[SBP\] \>= 150 mmHg and/or diastolic blood pressure \[DBP\] \>= 90 mmHg despite optimal medical management)
  * No clinically significant GI bleeding within 6 months of registration
  * No clinically significant gastrointestinal abnormalities that may increase the risk for gastrointestinal bleeding within 6 months of registration including, but not limited to: active peptic ulcer, known endoluminal metastatic lesion(s) with history of bleeding, inflammatory bowel disease, or other gastrointestinal conditions with increased risk of perforation
  * No GI perforation within 6 months of registration
  * No known tumor with invasion into the GI tract from the outside causing increased risk of perforation or bleeding within 28 days of registration
  * No radiologic or clinical evidence of pancreatitis
  * No known cavitary lung lesions
  * No known endobronchial lesions involving the main or lobar bronchi and/or lesions infiltrating major pulmonary vessels that increase the risk of pulmonary hemorrhage; (CT with contrast is recommended to evaluate such lesions)
  * No hemoptysis greater than 1/2 teaspoon (2.5 mL) or any other signs of pulmonary hemorrhage within the 3 months prior to registration
  * No known tumor invading or encasing any major blood vessels
  * No history of non-healing wounds or ulcers within 28 days of registration
  * No history of fracture within 28 days of registration
  * No brain metastases or cranial epidural disease unless adequately treated, stable, and off steroid support for at least 4 weeks prior to registration
  * No known medical condition causing an inability to swallow oral formulations of agents
  * No history of allergic reaction attributed to compounds of similar chemical or biological composition to cabozantinib/placebo
  * No "currently active" second malignancy other than non-melanoma skin cancers or cervical carcinoma in situ; patients are not considered to have a "currently active" malignancy if they have completed therapy and are free of disease for \>= 3 years
* Concomitant Medications

  * Other planned concurrent investigational agents or other tumor directed therapies (chemotherapy, radiation) are not allowed while on this study
  * Concurrent use of somatostatin analogs while on cabozantinib/placebo is allowed provided that the patient has been on a stable dose for at least two months
  * Full dose oral anticoagulation/antiplatelet therapy is not permitted; low dose aspirin =\< 81 mg/day is allowed; anticoagulation with therapeutic doses of low molecular weight heparin (LMWH) is allowed in patients who are on a stable dose of LMWH for at least 6 weeks prior to registration; treatment with warfarin is not allowed; anticoagulation in patients with brain metastases is not permitted
  * Chronic concomitant treatment with strong inhibitors of CYP3A4 is not allowed; patients must discontinue the drug at least 14 days prior to registration on the study
  * Chronic concomitant treatment with strong CYP3A4 inducers is not allowed; patients must discontinue the drug at least 14 days prior to registration on the study
* Not pregnant and not nursing

  * Women of childbearing potential must have a negative pregnancy test done =\< 14 days prior to registration
  * A female of childbearing potential is a sexually mature female who: 1) has not undergone a hysterectomy or bilateral oophorectomy; or 2) has not been naturally postmenopausal for at least 12 consecutive months (i.e. has had menses at any time in the preceding 12 consecutive months)
* Age \>= 18 years
* Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status: 0-2
* Absolute neutrophil count (ANC) \>= 1,500/mm\^3
* Hemoglobin \>= 9 g/dL
* Platelet count \>= 100,000/mm\^3
* Prothrombin time (PT)/ international normalized ratio (INR), partial thromboplastin time (PTT) \< 1.3 x upper limit of normal (ULN)
* Aspartate aminotransferase (AST)/ alanine aminotransferase (ALT) =\< 3 x ULN
* Total bilirubin =\< 1.5 x ULN

  * Except in the case of Gilbert disease, in which case total bilirubin must be =\< 3 x ULN
* Creatinine =\< 1.5 mg/dL OR creatinine clearance \>= 45 mL/min
* Albumin \>= 2.8 g/dL
* Potassium within normal limits (WNL)

  * Supplementation is acceptable to achieve a value WNL; in patients with low albumin levels, a corrected calcium value WNL is acceptable; in patients with abnormal thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH), if free T4 is normal and patient is clinically euthyroid, patient is eligible
* Phosphorus WNL

  * Supplementation is acceptable to achieve a value WNL; in patients with low albumin levels, a corrected calcium value WNL is acceptable; in patients with abnormal TSH, if free T4 is normal and patient is clinically euthyroid, patient is eligible
* Calcium WNL

  * Supplementation is acceptable to achieve a value WNL; in patients with low albumin levels, a corrected calcium value WNL is acceptable; in patients with abnormal TSH, if free T4 is normal and patient is clinically euthyroid, patient is eligible
* Magnesium WNL

  * Supplementation is acceptable to achieve a value WNL; in patients with low albumin levels, a corrected calcium value WNL is acceptable; in patients with abnormal TSH, if free T4 is normal and patient is clinically euthyroid, patient is eligible
* Urine protein to creatinine (UPC) ratio =\< 1
* QT interval corrected for heart rate using Fridericia's formula (QTcF) =\< 500 msec
* TSH WNL

  * Supplementation is acceptable to achieve a value WNL; in patients with low albumin levels, a corrected calcium value WNL is acceptable; in patients with abnormal TSH, if free T4 is normal and patient is clinically euthyroid, patient is eligible

publications.title: Phase 3 Trial of Cabozantinib to Treat Advanced Neuroendocrine Tumors.
publications.abstract_text: Treatment options for patients with advanced neuroendocrine tumors are limited. The efficacy of cabozantinib in the treatment of previously treated, progressive extrapancreatic or pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors is unclear.
publications.full_content: Full text links Cite Display options Display options Format Abstract PubMed PMID Abstract Background: Treatment options for patients with advanced neuroendocrine tumors are limited. The efficacy of cabozantinib in the treatment of previously treated, progressive extrapancreatic or pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors is unclear. Methods: We enrolled two independent cohorts of patients - those with extrapancreatic neuroendocrine tumors and those with pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors - who had received peptide receptor radionuclide therapy or targeted therapy or both. Patients were randomly assigned in a 2:1 ratio to receive cabozantinib at a dose of 60 mg daily or placebo. The primary end point was progression-free survival as assessed by blinded independent central review. Key secondary end points included objective response, overall survival, and safety. Results: In the cohort of 203 patients with extrapancreatic neuroendocrine tumors, the median progression-free survival with cabozantinib was 8.4 months, as compared with 3.9 months with placebo (stratified hazard ratio for progression or death, 0.38; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.25 to 0.59; P<0.001). In the cohort of 95 patients with pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors, the median progression-free survival with cabozantinib was 13.8 months, as compared with 4.4 months with placebo (stratified hazard ratio, 0.23; 95% CI, 0.12 to 0.42; P<0.001). The incidence of confirmed objective response with cabozantinib was 5% and 19% among patients with extrapancreatic and pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors, respectively, as compared with 0% with placebo. Grade 3 or higher adverse events were noted in 62 to 65% of the patients treated with cabozantinib, as compared with 23 to 27% of the patients who received placebo. Common treatment-related adverse events of grade 3 or higher included hypertension, fatigue, diarrhea, and thromboembolic events. Conclusions: Cabozantinib, as compared with placebo, significantly improved progression-free survival in patients with previously treated, progressive advanced extrapancreatic or pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors. Adverse events were consistent with the known safety profile of cabozantinib. (Funded by the National Cancer Institute and others; CABINET ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT03375320 .). evaluation.explanation: The study provides meaningful evidence for a subsequent line of therapy for this patient. Biologically, the patient's well-differentiated G2 ileal NET aligns with the study's extra-pancreatic NET (epNET) cohort. Clinically, the patient has progressed on SSA and recently completed PRRT; the CABINET trial specifically enrolled patients who had progressed after prior therapies, including PRRT (Lu-177-DOTATATE), making the study population directly representative of this patient's treatment history and future trajectory. Although the patient is currently responding to PRRT and considering surgery, she has metastatic disease that will likely eventually progress. The published Phase 3 results demonstrate a significant progression-free survival benefit (8.4 vs. 3.9 months) for Cabozantinib versus placebo in this setting. This establishes Cabozantinib as an evidence-based treatment option for the patient upon future disease progression, informing the long-term sequencing strategy.

relevant_trials.title: A Phase II Study of Ramucirumab With Somatostatin Analog Therapy in Patients With Advanced, Progressive Carcinoid Tumors
relevant_trials.brief_summary: This research study is evaluating the drug Ramucirumab as a possible treatment for Advanced, Progressive Carcinoid Tumors.
relevant_trials.detailed_description:
This research study is a Phase II clinical trial. The purpose of this study is to test the safety and effectiveness of ramucirumab in advanced, progressive carcinoid tumors.

Cancer cells can make growth factors that cause the abnormal growth of new blood vessels. Ramucirumab is an investigational drug which works by blocking a receptor for a vascular growth factor, thereby preventing new blood vessels from forming. This may stop the cancer from growing or spreading and the tumor cells may die.

The FDA (the U.S. Food and Drug Administration) has not approved Ramucirumab for treatment of Carcinoid Tumors.
relevant_trials.eligibility_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Participants must have histologically or cytologically confirmed low- to intermediate-grade neuroendocrine tumor (carcinoid tumor).
* Carcinoid tumors of any site are eligible. Patients with pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors are excluded.
* Participants must have measurable disease, defined as at least one lesion that can be accurately measured in at least one dimension (longest diameter to be recorded for non-nodal lesions and short axis for nodal lesions) as ≥20 mm with conventional techniques or as ≥10 mm with spiral CT scan, MRI, or calipers by clinical exam. See Section 10 for the evaluation of measurable disease.
* Locally advanced, unresectable or metastatic disease.
* Patients must have evidence of radiographic disease progression within the past 12 months. Progressive disease by RECIST criteria is not required.
* Age ≥ 18 years.
* ECOG performance status 0-1 (see Appendix A).
* Participants must have normal organ and marrow function as defined below:

  * absolute neutrophil count ≥1,000/ mm3
  * platelets ≥100,000/ mm3
  * hemoglobin ≥ 9 g/dL
  * total bilirubin ≤ 1.5 × institutional upper limit of normal
  * AST(SGOT)/ALT(SGPT) ≤ 3 × institutional upper limit of normal, or ≤ 5× institutional upper limit of normal in the setting of liver metastases
  * creatinine ≤ 1.5 × upper limit of normal
  * urinary protein ≤ 1+ on dipstick or routine urinalysis (if urine dipstick or routine urinalysis is 2+, a 24-hour urine collection for protein must demonstrate \<1000 mg of protein in 24 hours)
  * coagulation function Adequate coagulation function as defined by International Normalized Ratio (INR) ≤ 1.5 and a partial thromboplastin time (PTT) \< 1.5 x institutional upper limit of normal. Patients on full-dose anticoagulation must be on a stable dose (minimum duration 14 days) of oral anticoagulant or low molecular weight heparin.
  * The effects of ramucirumab on the developing human fetus are unknown. For this reason and because anti-antiangiogenic agents are known to be teratogenic, women of child-bearing potential and men must agree to use adequate contraception (hormonal or barrier method of birth control; abstinence) prior to study entry and for the duration of study participation. Should a woman become pregnant or suspect she is pregnant while she or her partner is participating in this study, she should inform her treating physician immediately. Men treated or enrolled on this protocol must also agree to use adequate contraception prior to the study, for the duration of study participation, and 4 months after completion of Ramucirumab administration.
* Ability to understand and the willingness to sign a written informed consent document.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Patients who have had chemotherapy or radiotherapy within 4 weeks prior to entering the study or those who have not recovered from adverse events due to agents administered more than 4 weeks earlier.
* Patients who have undergone major surgery within 28 days or subcutaneous venous access device placement within 7 days prior to study enrollment.
* Patients with elective or planned major surgery to be performed during the course of the clinical trial.
* Patients who are receiving any other investigational agents.
* Patients with any Grade 3-4 gastrointestinal bleeding within 3 months prior to enrollment.
* Patients with a history of deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, or any other significant thromboembolism (venous port or catheter thrombosis or superficial venous thrombosis are not considered "significant") during the 3 months prior to registration.
* Patients who have experienced any arterial thromboembolic events, including but not limited to myocardial infarction, transient ischemic attack, cerebrovascular accident, or unstable angina, within 6 months prior to enrollment.
* Patients with uncontrolled or poorly-controlled hypertension (\>160 mmHg systolic or \> 100 mmHg diastolic for \>4 weeks) despite standard medical management.
* Patients who have congestive heart failure (NYHA Class III or IV), sustained ventricular tachycardia, ventricular fibrillation, clinically significant bradycardia, advanced heart block within the six months preceding enrollment.
* Patients who have cirrhosis at a level of Child-Pugh B (or worse) or cirrhosis (any degree) and a history of hepatic encephalopathy or clinically meaningful ascites resulting from cirrhosis.
* Patients with a serious or nonhealing wound, ulcer, or bone fracture within 28 days prior to enrollment.
* Patients receiving chronic antiplatelet therapy, including aspirin, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs, including ibuprofen, naproxen, and others), dipyridamole or clopidogrel, or similar agents. Once-daily aspirin use (maximum dose 325 mg/day) is permitted.
* Patients with uncontrolled brain or leptomeningeal metastases, including patients who continue to require glucocorticoids for brain or leptomeningeal metastases.
* Patients with prior or concurrent malignancy except for the following: adequately treated basal cell or squamous cell skin cancer, or other adequately treated in situ cancer, or any other cancer from which the patient has been disease free for five years.
* Patients with symptomatic cholelithiasis.
* Patients who have any severe and/or uncontrolled medical conditions or other conditions that could affect their participation in the study such as:

  * Severely impaired lung function
  * Any active (acute or chronic) or uncontrolled infection/ disorders.
  * Nonmalignant medical illnesses that are uncontrolled or whose control may be jeopardized by the treatment with the study therapy
  * Psychiatric illness/social situations that would limit compliance with study requirement
* History of allergic reactions attributed to compounds of similar chemical or biologic composition to ramucirumab .
* Pregnant and breastfeeding women are excluded from this study because ramucirumab is associated with the potential for teratogenic or abortifacient effects. Because there is an unknown but potential risk for adverse events in nursing infants secondary to treatment of the mother with ramucirumab, breastfeeding should be discontinued if the mother is treated with ramucirumab. These potential risks may also apply to other agents used in this study.

publications.full_content: Full text links Cite Display options Display options Format Abstract PubMed PMID Abstract Objectives: Well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumors (NET) are highly vascular tumors characterized by their expression of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF). This trial investigated the activity of ramucirumab, a monoclonal antibody that targets VEGF receptor-2 (VEGFR-2) and inhibits activity of VEGF, in combination with somatostatin analog therapy in patients (pts) with advanced extra-pancreatic NET. Methods: We conducted a single-arm phase II trial enrolling pts with advanced, progressive extra-pancreatic NET. Patients were treated with ramucirumab 8 mg/kg intravenously on days 1 and 15 of each 28-day cycle. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS). Secondary endpoints toxicity, radiographic and biochemical tumor response rate, and overall survival (OS). Results: The trial enrolled 43 patients. Primary tumor sites included small intestine 20 (46%), lung 10 (23%), thymus 3 (7%), rectum 1(2%), kidney 1(2%), and unknown primary 8(18%). Median PFS was 14.2 months (95% CI, 9.0-25.6 months), and median OS was 24.9 months (95% CI, 20.7-43.1 months). Best response by RECIST 1.1: partial response 5% (95% CI, 0.6%-15.8%). Chromogranin A levels dropped by at least 50% in 10% of the 37 patients who had elevated levels at baseline. Most common all-grade adverse events included fatigue (84%) and hypertension (84%). Conclusion: Ramucirumab demonstrated efficacy and safety in this single-arm phase II trial. These findings support the continued evaluation of angiogenesis inhibitors in the treatment of NET. evaluation.explanation: The study provides meaningful clinical evidence for this patient's management. Biologically, the patient's condition (G2 well-differentiated Ileal NET with liver and peritoneal metastases) aligns perfectly with the study population of advanced extra-pancreatic NETs (46% small intestine). Clinically, while the patient is currently in partial response post-PRRT and considering surgery, she is young (39) and will likely require multiple lines of systemic therapy over her lifetime. The study evaluates Ramucirumab (a VEGFR-2 inhibitor) combined with SSA in patients with progressive disease (a status the patient met prior to PRRT). The published Phase II results demonstrate meaningful efficacy (median PFS 14.2 months, OS 24.9 months) and safety. This evidence validates the utility of angiogenesis inhibition as a therapeutic strategy for Si-NETs, offering a potential evidence-based option for future treatment lines (e.g., upon progression after PRRT/surgery), particularly given the limited standard options (mainly Everolimus) available for this subtype.

relevant_trials.title: Cabozantinib in Advanced Pancreatic Neuroendocrine and Carcinoid Tumors
relevant_trials.brief_summary:
Cabozantinib works by blocking the growth of new blood vessels that feed a tumor. In addition to blocking the formation of new blood cells in tumors, cabozantinib also blocks pathways that may be responsible for allowing cancers cells to become resistant to other "anti-angiogenic" drugs. Cabozantinib has been studied or is being study in research studies as a possible treatment for various types of cancer, including prostate cancer, brain cancer, thyroid cancer, lung cancer, and kidney cancer.

In this research study, the investigators wish to learn if cabozantinib is effective in treating patients with pancreatic neuroendocrine and carcinoid tumors.
relevant_trials.detailed_description:
Subjects will take cabozantinib orally, once per day, in cycles of 28 days.

During each cycle subjects will have the following procedures:

* Physical examination, including measurement of weight and vital signs
* Questions regarding any side effects
* Blood sample (about 1 tablespoon) for routine laboratory tests of blood cell counts, blood chemistries, organ function and blood clotting
* Blood sample (about 4 tablespoons) for research test to measure biomarkers to assess the response to study drug
* Urine sample for routine urine tests to monitor health

On Day 15 (beginning of week 3) during the first 3 cycles:

* Physical examination, including measurement of weight and vital signs
* Questions regarding any side effects
* Blood sample (about 1 tablespoon) for routine laboratory tests of blood cell counts, blood chemistries, organ function and blood clotting
* Blood sample (about 4 tablespoons) for research test to measure biomarkers to assess the response to study drug Subjects will receive a CT scan or MRI every two cycles (every two months) to evaluate disease.
relevant_trials.eligibility_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Locally unresectable or metastatic, histologically-confirmed, carcinoid or pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor. Tumors must be considered well- or moderately-differentiated. Patients with poorly differentiated neuroendocrine carcinoma or cell carcinoma are excluded from the study.
* A tumor sample is required for enrollment (except for patients diagnosed \> 7 years ago).
* Must have measurable disease by RECIST criteria
* Must have evidence of progressive disease within 12 months of study entry
* Prior or concurrent therapy with somatostatin analogs is permitted. If on somatostatin/octreotide, must be on a stable dose for at least two months.
* Age ≥ 18 years
* No major surgery or radiation in the prior 4 weeks prior to enrollment
* No prior therapy with cabozantinib
* ECOG Performance status ≤ 1
* Participants must have adequate organ and marrow function as defined below:

  * Absolute neutrophil count \> 1,500/mcL
  * Platelets \> 100,000/mcL
  * Total bilirubin \</= 1.5X normal institutional limits
  * AST (SGOT) and ALT (SGPT) \</=2.5x normal institutional limits, or \< 5x if liver metastases are present
  * Creatinine \</= 1.5x normal institutional limits or creatinine clearance \> 50mL/min
  * Urine Protein:Creatinine ratio of \<1
  * Lipase \< 1.5X upper limit of normal
  * Serum Albumin ≥ 2.8 g/dl
* Sexually active subjects must agree to use medically accepted methods of birth control during the course of the study and for 3 months following discontinuation of study treatments (excluding women who are not of child bearing potential and men who have been sterilized).
* Ability to understand and the willingness to sign a written informed consent document.

Exclusion Criteria

* Subjects receiving any other standard or investigational anticancer agents, with the exception of somatostatin/octreotide therapy. If patients has received prior cytotoxic chemotherapy, must be at least three weeks since last treatment before first dose of study treatment.
* Major surgery or radiation treatment \<4 weeks prior to enrollment. In addition, cannot have received radiation to the thorax or gastrointestinal tract within three months of the first dose of study treatment.
* Cannot have received radionuclide treatment within 6 weeks of first dose of study treatment.
* High grade or poorly differentiated neuroendocrine tumors
* Ongoing immunosuppression with systemic steroids or other immune modulator
* Presence of CNS metastatic disease
* Uncontrolled hypertension defined by SBP \> 140 or DBP \> 90 despite titration of anti hypertensive medications
* No uncontrolled intercurrent illness including, but not limited to, ongoing or active infection, symptomatic congestive heart failure, unstable angina pectoris, cardiac arrhythmia other than chronic atrial fibrillation, or psychiatric illness/social situations that would limit compliance with study requirements. Congestive heart failure or symptomatic coronary artery disease within 3 months prior to enrollment
* Cerebrovascular accident within prior 6 months
* The subject has a history of clinically significant hematemesis or a recent history of hemoptysis of \> 2.5 mL of red blood or other signs indicative of pulmonary hemorrhage or evidence of endobronchial lesion(s).
* The subject has a pulmonary lesion abutting or encasing a major blood vessel.
* Previous history of pulmonary embolism or deep venous thrombosis
* The subject requires concomitant treatment, in therapeutic doses, with anticoagulants such as warfarin or Coumadin-related agents, heparin, thrombin or FXa inhibitors, and antiplatelet agents (eg, clopidogrel). Low dose aspirin (≤ 81 mg/day), low-dose warfarin (≤ 1 mg/day), and prophylactic Low Molecular Weight Heparin (LMWH) are permitted.
* At the time of screening, active peptic ulcer disease or active inflammatory bowel disease (including ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease), diverticulitis, cholecystitis, symptomatic cholangitis, or appendicitis.
* History of abdominal fistula, gastrointestinal perforation, bowel obstruction, gastric outlet obstruction, or intra-abdominal abscess within six months of study enrollment.
* History of GI surgery within the past 28 days. If \>28 days since GI surgery, must have confirmation of complete healing before initiating treatment with study drug.
* Other disorders associated with a high risk of fistula formation, including PEG tube placement within 3 months before the first dose of study therapy or concurrent evidence of intraluminal tumor involving the trachea or esophagus.
* Other clinically significant disorders such as:

  * Active infection requiring systemic treatment
  * Serious non-healing wound/ulcer/bone fracture
  * History of organ transplant
  * Concurrent uncompensated hypothyroidism or thyroid dysfunction
  * History of major surgery within 4 weeks or minor surgical procedures within one week before randomization
* The subject has a corrected QT interval calculated by the Fridericia formula \> 500ms within 28 days before randomization.
* Severely impaired lung function
* Concurrent malignancy (other than non-melanoma skin cancer) diagnosed within the past 3 years or any currently active malignancy
* Pregnant women are excluded from this study due to the potential for teratogenic or abortifacient effects. Because there is an unknown but potential risk of adverse events in nursing infants secondary to treatment of the mother with the treatment protocol, breastfeeding should be discontinued if the mother is treated on protocol.

evaluation.explanation: The study is relevant because it evaluates Cabozantinib in patients with advanced carcinoid tumors (neuroendocrine tumors), which aligns with the patient's diagnosis of a well-differentiated G2 ileal NET (historically classified as carcinoid). Although the patient is currently responding to PRRT and considering surgery, she has metastatic disease that progressed on prior somatostatin analogs. The study (NCT01466036) is a Phase II trial that included a cohort of 41 patients with carcinoid tumors, providing evidence of efficacy for Cabozantinib in this population. This evidence is clinically meaningful for informing future treatment sequencing, as Cabozantinib represents a potential subsequent systemic therapy option should the disease progress after PRRT and surgery. The inclusion of well-differentiated tumors and the allowance of prior SSA therapy further support the transferability of these findings to the patient's clinical scenario.

all_evaluations.explanation: The study does not provide meaningful evidence to guide therapy recommendations for this patient. Although the patient’s diagnosis of a G2 well-differentiated GEP-NET aligns with the study’s inclusion criteria, the Phase II trial of Avelumab demonstrated no objective responses (0% ORR) and limited progression-free survival (median 3.3 months) in this population. Consequently, the study fails to establish Avelumab as a viable treatment approach. For a patient with a low proliferation index (Ki-67 2-6%) who is currently responding to PRRT, immunotherapy is not a standard consideration, and the negative trial results reinforce that it should not be pursued. Therefore, the evidence does not offer actionable positive insights for the patient’s current management or the decision regarding surgery versus PRRT sequencing. The study fails the Treatment Context and Evidence Relevance criteria as the intervention proved ineffective.
all_evaluations.trial_title: Avelumab in G2-3 NET

all_evaluations.explanation: This study is a broad observational registry designed to collect real-world data across various advanced malignancies rather than a clinical trial evaluating a specific intervention for Neuroendocrine Tumors (NETs). While the patient meets the general inclusion criteria for advanced malignancy, the provided publications are methodological papers discussing real-world evidence frameworks, next-generation sequencing, and master protocols, rather than reporting clinical outcomes. There are no specific efficacy or safety results regarding PRRT, surgery, or their sequencing in midgut NETs. Therefore, the study fails to provide actionable clinical evidence to inform the specific treatment decision between PRRT and surgery for this patient (Criterion 3 not met).

all_evaluations.explanation: The study fails the Treatment Context and Clinical Applicability criterion. While the disease biology (metastatic G2 GEP-NET) aligns, the patient has already experienced disease progression on long-acting Somatostatin Analogs (SSA) and has subsequently responded to PRRT. This observational study evaluates the efficacy (Time to Disease Progression) of Lanreotide in a community setting for patients who are largely SSA-naïve or stable, explicitly excluding those who progressed prior to study entry. evaluation_results.explanation: The study is not relevant because the intervention (Tamoxifen) targets a specific biomarker (Estrogen/Progesterone Receptor expression) that is not reported for this patient. Unlike SSTR status, which is highly prevalent in well-differentiated NETs, ER/PR expression is found in only a minority (~30%) of cases, so **Disease/Biology Alignment** cannot be established or assumed. Furthermore, the **Treatment Context** is inapplicable; the patient has achieved a partial response to PRRT and is currently evaluating surgical resection, whereas the study addresses a salvage setting for patients with no established treatment options. Finally, the **Evidence Quality and Relevance** is low for this case, as the study demonstrated only "modest antitumor effects" (median PFS 7.9 months) in a small, biomarker-selected cohort, offering no actionable insights for the current decision between surgery and PRRT sequencing.
evaluation_results.trial_title: Study of Tamoxifen in Well Differentiated Neuroendocrine Tumors and Hormone Receptor Positive Expression

evaluation_results.explanation: The study provides meaningful clinical evidence relevant to this patient's long-term management. Biologically, the patient's G2 ileal neuroendocrine tumor (Si-NET) aligns with the study's extrapancreatic NET (epNET) cohort, which enrolled patients with progressive G1-G2 NETs. Clinically, while the patient is currently responding to PRRT and considering surgery, she has metastatic incurable disease and has previously progressed on SSAs. Given her young age (39), she will likely require multiple lines of systemic therapy over her lifetime. The published results (Halperin et al., 2022) demonstrate that the combination of atezolizumab and bevacizumab has clinical activity in epNETs (ORR 15%, median PFS 14.2 months). This evidence informs future therapy recommendations by validating a potential non-standard systemic treatment option to consider should the patient progress after PRRT and surgery, or if she becomes refractory to other standard therapies.
evaluation_results.trial_title: Atezolizumab and Bevacizumab in Treating Patients With Rare Solid Tumors

evaluation_results.explanation: The study does not provide meaningful evidence for this patient for two key reasons. First, the provided publication is a methodology and design paper (Protocol) without reported efficacy or safety results; it describes what the trial *will* investigate rather than providing outcomes to guide decision-making. Second, there is a significant population mismatch regarding treatment history and resistance. The patient has documented disease progression on standard Somatostatin Analogues (SSAs) and has received PRRT. The SORENTO trial specifically excludes patients with progression on SSAs and those who have received prior PRRT, focusing instead on establishing superiority in an earlier, SSA-sensitive or treatment-naive setting. Consequently, no evidence is available from this source to inform the management of an SSA-refractory, post-PRRT patient.
evaluation_results.trial_title: A Trial to Assess Efficacy and Safety of Octreotide Subcutaneous Depot in Patients with GEP-NET

evaluation_results.explanation: The study does not provide meaningful evidence for the specific therapeutic decision facing this patient. While the disease biology (NET) aligns, this is a diagnostic imaging study evaluating the utility of 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT for diagnosis and management changes, specifically focusing on initial diagnosis in the provided publication results. The patient has already undergone SSTR-PET imaging (Ga-68-DOTATOC), has a confirmed diagnosis, and has already received PRRT with a partial response. The current clinical question regarding the sequencing of therapy (surgery vs. further PRRT) requires therapeutic efficacy data comparing these modalities or evaluating their combination. This study offers diagnostic yield statistics but does not provide data on survival, recurrence, or treatment efficacy that would inform the choice between surgical resection and systemic therapy in a post-PRRT setting.
evaluation_results.trial_title: 68Ga-DOTATATE PET for Management of Neuroendocrine Tumors

evaluation_results.explanation: The study does not meet the Disease/Biology Alignment criterion. The patient has a well-differentiated G2 neuroendocrine tumor (NET) with a low Ki-67 index (2-6%), whereas the study (NCT02113800) specifically targets patients with poorly differentiated neuroendocrine carcinoma (NEC), NEC G3, or NET G3 (high-grade). The biological behavior and treatment responses of low-grade G2 NETs differ significantly from the high-grade G3 populations investigated in this trial. Furthermore, the Treatment Context is inapplicable; the study evaluates Everolimus as a second-line therapy after platinum-based chemotherapy failure, a setting not relevant to this patient who has received SSA and PRRT and is currently evaluating surgical options. While Everolimus is approved for G2 NETs based on other trials (e.g., RADIANT-4), evidence from this specific study on G3/NEC populations does not inform the clinical decision regarding surgery versus PRRT for a G2 patient.

evaluation_results.explanation: The study fails all criteria for relevance. First, regarding disease alignment, the study focuses on the diagnosis of solid lesions in the **pancreas** (specifically differentiating pancreatic cancer from other lesions like pancreatic NETs or pancreatitis), whereas the patient has a confirmed **ileal** (midgut) neuroendocrine tumor. Second, regarding treatment context, the study evaluates a diagnostic tool (AI-assisted EUS) intended for initial characterization of lesions, while the patient has an established diagnosis and is currently facing a therapeutic decision (sequencing of PRRT and surgery). Finally, the evidence provided relates solely to diagnostic accuracy and offers no data on treatment efficacy, safety, or survival outcomes that could inform the choice between surgery and systemic therapy for this patient.

evaluation_results.explanation: The study does not meet the criteria for disease alignment or clinical applicability. The study evaluates the necessity of right-sided hemicolectomy versus appendectomy to prevent recurrence in early-stage appendiceal disease. This evidence is not transferable to the patient's scenario, which involves decision-making regarding cytoreductive surgery for established metastatic ileal disease following PRRT. The biological behavior and surgical management of localized appendiceal NETs differ significantly from metastatic small bowel NETs, rendering the study's findings on prophylactic lymphadenectomy irrelevant to this patient's treatment plan.
evaluation_results.trial_title: Distant Metastases and Long-Term Survival After Complete Resection of Neuroendocrine Tumors of the Appendix

evaluation_results.explanation: The study provides meaningful evidence for this patient with a G2 well-differentiated ileal neuroendocrine tumor (NET) and SSTR-positive liver/peritoneal metastases. Biologically, the patient matches the study population (progressive, SSTR-positive NETs). Clinically, the study evaluates the efficacy and safety of 177Lu-Octreotate PRRT, the specific therapy this patient received after progressing on somatostatin analogs. The published results demonstrate an objective response rate of 23.1% and stable disease in 33.3%, with a favorable safety profile using a personalized dosimetry approach. This evidence directly supports the clinical utility of PRRT in this setting, validating the decision to administer PRRT for progressive disease. Furthermore, the study's insights into dosimetry-based optimization and maintenance cycles could inform future management if re-treatment or consolidation therapy is considered following the patient's partial response.
evaluation_results.trial_title: Personalized PRRT of Neuroendocrine Tumors

evaluation_results.explanation: The study does not provide meaningful evidence to guide therapy for this patient. While the study included neuroendocrine neoplasms (NENs) of any origin, the published results (PMID: 36255391) demonstrated a significant difference in efficacy based on primary site, with a high response rate in Lung NENs (64%) compared to a very low response rate in non-lung NENs (~12%). This patient has a well-differentiated Ileal (midgut) NET, a subtype biologically known to be less responsive to Temozolomide and immunotherapy compared to lung or pancreatic NETs. Furthermore, the clinical context does not align: the patient is currently in partial response following PRRT and is being evaluated for surgery, whereas the study evaluates a salvage systemic therapy regimen (Nivolumab plus Temozolomide) for patients with progressive disease. Given the poor efficacy signal for this specific tumor subtype and the mismatch in clinical setting (responding vs. refractory), this study does not offer a viable treatment recommendation.
evaluation_results.trial_title: Nivolumab and Temozolomide in Treating Patients With Recurrent or Refractory Small-Cell Lung Cancer or Advanced Neuroendocrine Cancer

This study is purely diagnostic, validating plasma 5-HIAA and overnight urinary 5-HIAA as methodological alternatives to 24-hour urinary 5-HIAA for monitoring. Consequently, the published results regarding biomarker measurement methodology offer no actionable insights to resolve the tumor board's question about whether to proceed with upfront surgery or PRRT.
evaluation_results.trial_title: Diagnostic Performances of Urine and Plasma 5-hydroxyindolacetic Acid (5HIAA) Values in Patients With Small-intestine Neuroendocrine Tumors

This distinction is clinically critical because midgut NETs are biologically distinct and generally considered resistant to the cytotoxic chemotherapy regimens (alkylating agents or oxaliplatin) evaluated in this study, unlike pancreatic NETs where such therapies are standard. Consequently, the study's findings regarding MGMT status as a predictor for chemotherapy response are not transferable to this patient. evaluation_results.explanation: The study is relevant because it aligns with the patient's diagnosis of SSTR-positive small intestine NET (Si-NET) and the current clinical consideration of cytoreductive surgery. The published results (PMID 38652200) demonstrate that 68Ga-DOTATOC radio-guided surgery (RGS) significantly improves the intraoperative detection of occult lesions, particularly lymph nodes, with high sensitivity (89.3%) and specificity. Since the patient has nodal (pN1) and peritoneal (pM1) involvement and is being evaluated for surgery following a partial response to PRRT, evidence supporting techniques that enhance the completeness of resection is directly applicable to the surgical planning and the assessment of resectability. Although the patient has received prior PRRT, she remains SSTR-positive (evidenced by response), making the biological rationale for RGS valid. This evidence informs the tumor board's decision by highlighting methods to optimize surgical cytoreduction, a critical component of the proposed multimodal treatment strategy.

evaluation_results.explanation: This prospective Phase II study (LUMEN) is highly relevant as it evaluates the efficacy and safety of 177Lu-DOTATATE (PRRT) in patients with SSA-refractory advanced GEP-NETs, directly matching the patient's diagnosis (Ileal NET G2) and clinical history prior to her recent treatment. The published results demonstrate a 30% partial response rate and a median progression-free survival of 28 months, providing strong evidence supporting the decision to initiate PRRT in this patient following SSA progression. Furthermore, the study identifies dosimetric and volumetric predictors of response, which validates the observed partial response in this patient and offers prognostic context. While the study excludes patients with curative resectable tumors, it establishes the baseline efficacy of PRRT, which is crucial for the tumor board when weighing the benefits of systemic therapy against upfront or delayed surgical consolidation in the setting of metastatic disease.
evaluation_results.trial_title: 177Lutetium-octreotate Treatment Prediction Using Multimodality Imaging in Refractory NETs

Consequently, the study provides evidence that dual checkpoint inhibition (ipilimumab plus nivolumab) is ineffective for the patient's disease biology. evaluation_results.explanation: The study provides meaningful evidence for a subsequent line of therapy for this patient. Biologically, the patient's well-differentiated G2 ileal NET aligns with the study's extra-pancreatic NET (epNET) cohort. Clinically, the patient has progressed on SSA and recently completed PRRT; the CABINET trial specifically enrolled patients who had progressed after prior therapies, including PRRT (Lu-177-DOTATATE), making the study population directly representative of this patient's treatment history and future trajectory. Although the patient is currently responding to PRRT and considering surgery, she has metastatic disease that will likely eventually progress. The published Phase 3 results demonstrate a significant progression-free survival benefit (8.4 vs. 3.9 months) for Cabozantinib versus placebo in this setting. This establishes Cabozantinib as an evidence-based treatment option for the patient upon future disease progression, informing the long-term sequencing strategy.
evaluation_results.trial_title: Testing Cabozantinib in Patients With Advanced Pancreatic Neuroendocrine and Carcinoid Tumors

evaluation_results.explanation: The study provides meaningful clinical evidence for this patient's management. Biologically, the patient's condition (G2 well-differentiated Ileal NET with liver and peritoneal metastases) aligns perfectly with the study population of advanced extra-pancreatic NETs (46% small intestine). Clinically, while the patient is currently in partial response post-PRRT and considering surgery, she is young (39) and will likely require multiple lines of systemic therapy over her lifetime. The study evaluates Ramucirumab (a VEGFR-2 inhibitor) combined with SSA in patients with progressive disease (a status the patient met prior to PRRT). The published Phase II results demonstrate meaningful efficacy (median PFS 14.2 months, OS 24.9 months) and safety. This evidence validates the utility of angiogenesis inhibition as a therapeutic strategy for Si-NETs, offering a potential evidence-based option for future treatment lines (e.g., upon progression after PRRT/surgery), particularly given the limited standard options (mainly Everolimus) available for this subtype.
evaluation_results.trial_title: A Phase II Study of Ramucirumab With Somatostatin Analog Therapy in Patients With Advanced, Progressive Carcinoid Tumors

evaluation_results.explanation: The study does not provide meaningful evidence for this patient's therapy recommendations. First, the disease biology does not align: the patient has a midgut (ileal) NET, whereas the study specifically enrolled only patients with foregut NETs (thymic, bronchopulmonary, gastric, duodenal, pancreatic). Second, the study results were negative; the combination of ribociclib and everolimus demonstrated high toxicity (92% grade ≥2 myelosuppression) and no objective responses were observed, leading investigators to conclude the regimen had insufficient activity to warrant further investigation. Therefore, the study does not offer a viable treatment option or actionable evidence to inform the patient's current clinical decision between surgery and PRRT.
evaluation_results.trial_title: A Study of LEE011 With Everolimus in Patients With Advanced Neuroendocrine Tumors

evaluation_results.explanation: While the study includes a cohort (Cohort 5) that perfectly aligns with the patient's diagnosis of well-differentiated digestive NET (G1/G2) and clinical history (progression on SSA and PRRT), the provided published results are limited to the Adrenocortical Carcinoma (ACC) cohort. There are no specific efficacy or safety data (e.g., ORR, PFS) reported for the neuroendocrine tumor cohort in the provided inputs. Without outcomes specific to the NET population, the evidence is not currently actionable or transferable to guide treatment recommendations for this patient, as results from ACC cannot be extrapolated to well-differentiated NETs.
evaluation_results.trial_title: Trial of Cabozantinib Plus Atezolizumab in Advanced and Progressive Neoplasms of the Endocrine System. The CABATEN Study

evaluation_results.explanation: The study does not meet the Disease/Biology Alignment criterion. The patient has a well-differentiated G2 neuroendocrine tumor (NET) of the ileum with a low Ki-67 index (2-6%), whereas the PRECISION-NEC study (NCT04452292) focuses exclusively on high-grade neuroendocrine carcinomas (HG-NEC), specifically Large Cell Neuroendocrine Carcinoma (LCNEC). These are distinct biological entities with different genetic drivers (e.g., TP53/RB1 mutations in NEC vs. DAXX/ATRX or MEN1 in NETs) and treatment paradigms. Consequently, the study's investigation into NGS-based stratification for chemotherapy (platinum-based regimens) in aggressive carcinomas provides no clinical applicability or transferable evidence for a patient with a well-differentiated tumor currently responding to PRRT and evaluating surgical options.
evaluation_results.trial_title: Next Generation Sequencing-Based Stratification of Front Line Treatment of HighGrade Neuroendocrine Carcinoma

evaluation_results.explanation: The study does not provide meaningful evidence for therapy recommendations. While the disease biology (SSTR-positive NET) aligns, the study fails on Treatment Context and Evidence Quality. This is a technical imaging study designed to develop algorithms for simultaneous dual-tracer PET/CT acquisition, not a therapeutic trial evaluating clinical outcomes or treatment efficacy. The patient has already undergone standard SSTR-PET imaging and received PRRT, making the technical imaging focus irrelevant to the current decision regarding surgical resection versus systemic therapy sequencing. Furthermore, the study explicitly excludes patients who have received prior SSTR-targeted therapy (which this patient has), and no published results regarding therapeutic efficacy or clinical management are available to guide the tumor board's decision.
evaluation_results.trial_title: Dual-Tracer Theranostic PET

evaluation_results.explanation: The study does not provide meaningful evidence for the patient's therapy recommendations. While the disease biology aligns (GEP-NET), the study (NUTRIGETNE) is a non-interventional, cross-sectional observational study focused solely on the epidemiological assessment of nutritional status and malnutrition prevalence in Spain. It does not evaluate the efficacy, safety, or sequencing of anti-tumor therapies such as PRRT or surgery. Consequently, it fails to address the patient's specific clinical question regarding the choice between upfront surgery versus PRRT (or post-PRRT surgery). Additionally, no specific published results regarding therapeutic outcomes are provided. Therefore, the study lacks the necessary treatment context and evidence relevance to inform the therapeutic decision-making process for this patient.
evaluation_results.trial_title: Nutrition in Gastroenteropancreatic Neuroendocrine Tumor

evaluation_results.explanation: The study is relevant because it evaluates Cabozantinib in patients with advanced carcinoid tumors (neuroendocrine tumors), which aligns with the patient's diagnosis of a well-differentiated G2 ileal NET (historically classified as carcinoid). Although the patient is currently responding to PRRT and considering surgery, she has metastatic disease that progressed on prior somatostatin analogs. The study (NCT01466036) is a Phase II trial that included a cohort of 41 patients with carcinoid tumors, providing evidence of efficacy for Cabozantinib in this population. This evidence is clinically meaningful for informing future treatment sequencing, as Cabozantinib represents a potential subsequent systemic therapy option should the disease progress after PRRT and surgery. The inclusion of well-differentiated tumors and the allowance of prior SSA therapy further support the transferability of these findings to the patient's clinical scenario.
evaluation_results.trial_title: Cabozantinib in Advanced Pancreatic Neuroendocrine and Carcinoid Tumors

evaluation_results.explanation: The study does not provide meaningful evidence to inform therapy recommendations for this patient. While the disease biology (metastatic well-differentiated NET) aligns, the study is a Phase I trial evaluating the safety and dosimetry of an investigational somatostatin *antagonist* (177Lu-DOTA-JR11/Satoreotide Tetraxetan). The patient has already achieved a partial response to standard (agonist) PRRT and is currently evaluating the timing of surgery versus systemic therapy. Evidence from an early-phase safety study of an experimental agent does not guide the clinical decision regarding surgical resection or the sequencing of standard PRRT, nor does it provide a currently accessible alternative for a patient responding to standard of care.
evaluation_results.trial_title: Theranostics of Radiolabeled Somatostatin Antagonists 68Ga-DOTA-JR11 and 177Lu-DOTA-JR11 in Patients With Neuroendocrine Tumors

evaluation_results.explanation: This study does not provide meaningful evidence to guide the treatment decision for this patient. While the disease biology aligns (GEP-NET eligible for PRRT), the study fails the evidence relevance criterion. It is a Phase 4 post-authorization safety study focusing exclusively on the safety profile (serum potassium levels) of the arginine/lysine co-infusion used for renal protection during PRRT, rather than the efficacy or sequencing of the PRRT itself. The patient's clinical question involves the strategic sequencing of PRRT versus surgery (upfront vs. delayed), which this study does not address. Additionally, the provided data indicates no published results are available. Therefore, the study offers no actionable clinical insights regarding tumor control or survival outcomes necessary to inform the specific therapeutic recommendation.
evaluation_results.trial_title: Post-Authorization Safety Study (PASS) of LysaKare® in Adult Gastroenteropancreatic Neuroendocrine Tumor (GEP-NET) Patients

evaluation_results.explanation: The study does not provide meaningful evidence for this patient's care. While the patient has a neuroendocrine tumor, the Phase 2 study of ONC201 demonstrated clinical benefit primarily in pheochromocytoma-paraganglioma (PC-PG) and desmoplastic small round cell tumors (DSRCT), driven by specific DRD2 overexpression not typically characteristic of well-differentiated ileal NETs (Si-NETs). In the "other NETs" cohort (n=12), the only objective response occurred in a DSRCT patient, suggesting the efficacy is not transferable to the patient's subtype. Furthermore, the patient is currently responding to standard-of-care PRRT and is being evaluated for surgery; an experimental agent with no demonstrated efficacy in Si-NETs does not inform the decision between PRRT and surgery or offer a viable alternative line of therapy. Therefore, the study fails the criteria for disease alignment and clinical applicability.
evaluation_results.trial_title: Phase 2 Study of ONC201 in Neuroendocrine Tumors

evaluation_results.explanation: The study does not meet the criteria for disease alignment or evidence quality. The patient has a well-differentiated ileal (midgut) NET, whereas this study evaluates sunitinib specifically in pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (pNETs). These subtypes differ biologically and in treatment responsiveness; while sunitinib is established for pNETs, it is not a standard treatment for midgut NETs. Furthermore, the provided study data indicates 'No publications with results found' and cites irrelevant abstracts regarding pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) and general hypertension, offering no actionable efficacy or safety data. Therefore, the study provides no meaningful evidence to inform the decision between surgery and PRRT for this patient's ileal NET.
evaluation_results.trial_title: The Safety And Efficacy Of Sunitinib In Chinese Patients With Progressive Advanced Or Metastatic Well-Differentiated Unresectable Pancreatic Neuroendocrine Tumors

evaluation_results.explanation: The study fails the disease alignment and clinical applicability criteria. It evaluates the combination of cediranib (VEGF inhibitor) and olaparib (PARP inhibitor) specifically in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC). This is a biologically distinct malignancy from the patient's well-differentiated ileal neuroendocrine tumor (Si-NET). The study's population, treatment interventions, and outcomes are not transferable to a female patient with a G2 NET, nor does the study address the relevant clinical question regarding the sequencing of PRRT and surgery.
evaluation_results.trial_title: Testing Two Oral Drugs Combination (Cediranib and Olaparib) Compared to a Single Drug (Olaparib) for Men With Advanced Prostate Cancer

evaluation_results.explanation: The NETTER-2 trial does not provide meaningful evidence for this specific patient due to a significant mismatch in tumor biology and treatment setting. The patient has a 'low' Grade 2 ileal NET with a Ki-67 index of 2–6%, whereas NETTER-2 specifically enrolled patients with 'high' Grade 2 (Ki-67 ≥10%) and Grade 3 tumors to evaluate upfront PRRT in a more aggressive biological subset. Furthermore, the patient received PRRT as a second-line therapy after progression on somatostatin analogs (SSA), a sequence supported by the NETTER-1 trial, whereas NETTER-2 investigated PRRT as a first-line treatment in newly diagnosed patients. Extrapolating NETTER-2 results to a patient with low proliferation indices (Ki-67 <10%) is not clinically appropriate, as the risk-benefit profile and standard of care (SSA first-line) differ for this indolent population.
evaluation_results.trial_title: Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Lutathera in Patients With Grade 2 and Grade 3 Advanced GEP-NET

evaluation_results.explanation: This study does not provide meaningful evidence for the patient's care. The patient has a metastatic ileal neuroendocrine tumor (Si-NET), whereas this study (NCT01794793) is a rollover access program specifically for patients with Cushing's Disease or Acromegaly who were previously enrolled in Novartis-sponsored trials for those conditions. The published results focus exclusively on long-term safety and efficacy in pituitary disorders, which is biologically distinct from the patient's gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine malignancy. Furthermore, the study functions as a compassionate use/extension mechanism for patients already on pasireotide from prior specific trials, making the treatment context inapplicable to this patient who has progressed on standard SSAs and is currently evaluating post-PRRT surgical options. Consequently, the study fails the criteria for disease alignment and clinical applicability.
evaluation_results.trial_title: Study to Allow Access to Pasireotide for Patients Benefiting From Pasireotide Treatment in Novartis-sponsored Studies

evaluation_results.explanation: The study does not meet the criteria for clinical applicability or evidence relevance for this specific patient. While the disease biology (neuroendocrine tumor) aligns, the study evaluates telotristat ethyl (Xermelo) specifically for the management of uncontrolled carcinoid syndrome (CS) diarrhea. The patient is reported to be in 'good clinical conditions' with no mention of refractory carcinoid syndrome symptoms, and the primary clinical question addresses the sequencing of antiproliferative therapies (PRRT vs. surgery) for tumor control. Telotristat ethyl is a supportive care agent for symptom management and does not have established antiproliferative efficacy that would influence the decision between surgery and systemic therapy. Consequently, the study's evidence regarding symptom control outcomes is not actionable for the current decision-making process regarding tumor burden management.
evaluation_results.trial_title: Real-world Evidence Study EvaLuating PAtient-Reported Outcomes With XERMELO

evaluation_results.explanation: The study does not provide meaningful evidence for this patient because of a fundamental mismatch in treatment context. The patient has SSA-refractory disease (progressed on prior long-acting SSA) and has subsequently received PRRT. The study (NCT01253161) evaluates Pasireotide LAR exclusively in a *treatment-naïve* population, explicitly excluding patients with prior SSA exposure. Efficacy data (PFS of 11 months) derived from treatment-naïve patients cannot be extrapolated to guide therapy in a heavily pre-treated, refractory setting. Furthermore, the study does not address the patient's current clinical decision regarding post-PRRT surgery versus systemic maintenance. Therefore, the results are not transferable to this patient's advanced clinical scenario.
evaluation_results.trial_title: Study of Pasireotide Long Acting Release (LAR) in Patients With Metastatic Neuroendocrine Tumors (NETs)

evaluation_results.explanation: The study does not provide meaningful evidence for this patient because it focuses exclusively on neuroendocrine tumors of the lung and thymus (thoracic NETs), whereas the patient has a well-differentiated ileal (midgut) NET. In neuroendocrine oncology, the primary site is a critical determinant of biology and treatment response, and evidence from lung-specific trials is not extrapolated to midgut NETs, particularly when abundant site-specific data (e.g., RADIANT-4 for GI NETs) already exists. Furthermore, the study evaluates Pasireotide (a somatostatin analog not standardly used in midgut NETs) and Everolimus in a thoracic population; while Everolimus is a valid systemic option for the patient's disease, the clinical evidence supporting its use in ileal NETs is derived from different trials, not the LUNA study.
evaluation_results.trial_title: 3-arm Trial to Evaluate Pasireotide LAR/Everolimus Alone/in Combination in Patients With Lung/Thymus NET - LUNA Trial

evaluation_results.explanation: The study is not relevant because it specifically evaluates the safety and dosimetry of 177Lu-DOTATATE in adolescents (12–17 years old) to bridge established adult data to a pediatric population. The patient is a 39-year-old adult. While the disease biology (SSTR-positive GEP-NET) aligns, the study population is distinct, and the findings regarding adolescent pharmacokinetics and safety do not inform treatment decisions for an adult patient. Robust Phase III evidence for PRRT in adults (e.g., NETTER-1, NETTER-2) already exists and serves as the standard of care; therefore, this small pediatric safety study offers no actionable clinical insights for this specific patient scenario.
evaluation_results.trial_title: Study to Evaluate Safety and Dosimetry of Lutathera in Adolescent Patients With GEP-NETs and PPGLs

evaluation_results.explanation: The study is not relevant because it fails the treatment context and evidence relevance criteria. While the disease biology (metastatic WDNET) aligns, the study evaluates patient preference and pain scores between two first-line Somatostatin Analogs (Octreotide LAR vs. Lanreotide) in patients initiating therapy. This patient has already progressed on SSA therapy and has subsequently completed PRRT. The study provides no evidence regarding the efficacy of PRRT, the role of cytoreductive surgery, or the sequencing of these modalities (the primary clinical question). Evidence concerning the choice of first-line SSA is not actionable for a patient who is SSA-refractory and currently evaluating surgical intervention following PRRT response.
evaluation_results.trial_title: A Study to Evaluate Patient Experience in the Therapy of Neuroendocrine Tumors Treated With Octreotide Long Acting Release Versus Lanreotide

evaluation_results.explanation: The study does not meet the criteria for disease alignment or clinical applicability. First, the patient has a well-differentiated ileal neuroendocrine tumor (Si-NET), whereas the study is specifically restricted to pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (PNETs), which have distinct biological drivers and treatment responses. Second, the study investigates Sapanisertib in patients with rapalog-resistant disease (refractory to prior mTOR inhibitors), while this patient is mTOR-inhibitor naïve and currently evaluating surgery versus PRRT. Finally, the study was terminated early due to a lack of objective responses (0% response rate in Stage 1), meaning the intervention demonstrated no efficacy even in the target population. Consequently, a negative trial in a biologically distinct tumor subtype offers no actionable evidence to guide therapeutic decision-making for this patient's care.
evaluation_results.trial_title: Sapanisertib in Treating Patients With Metastatic or Refractory Pancreatic Neuroendocrine Tumor That Cannot Be Removed by Surgery

evaluation_results.explanation: The study does not meet the Disease/Biology Alignment criterion. It evaluates Nivolumab plus platinum-doublet chemotherapy specifically for patients with high-grade (G3) neuroendocrine neoplasms (Ki-67 >20%), whereas the patient has a well-differentiated G2 neuroendocrine tumor with a low Ki-67 index (2-6%). This represents a fundamental biological mismatch, as the aggressive cytotoxic and immunotherapy regimen tested targets rapidly proliferating cells and is not clinically applicable or biologically rational for indolent G2 NETs. Consequently, the study provides no transferable evidence for the patient's current treatment scenario (post-PRRT, considering surgery) or potential alternative systemic therapies.
evaluation_results.trial_title: Platinum-doublet Chemotherapy and Nivolumab for the Treatment of Subjects With Neuroendocrine Neoplasms (NENs) of the Gastroenteropancreatic (GEP) Tract or of Unknown (UK) Origin.

evaluation_results.explanation: While the study aligns with the patient's disease biology (metastatic carcinoid/NET) and explores a potential systemic therapy (regorafenib) that could be relevant in later-line settings, it fails the evidence quality and relevance criterion. The provided study data explicitly states that no publications or detailed findings are available. Without published results regarding efficacy (PFS, response rates) or safety, this completed Phase 2 trial offers no actionable clinical evidence to inform treatment recommendations or guide decision-making for this patient's current scenario (post-PRRT management) or future lines of therapy.
evaluation_results.trial_title: Regorafenib in Treating Patients With Advanced or Metastatic Neuroendocrine Tumors

evaluation_results.explanation: The study does not meet the criteria for disease alignment or evidence availability. First, the patient has an Ileal (midgut) NET, whereas the study specifically recruits patients with Pancreatic NETs (pNETs); these subtypes have distinct biological behaviors and trial landscapes, making the specific safety/efficacy data from a pNET cohort less transferable to an ileal primary. Second, no published results or findings are available for this completed Phase IV study, meaning there is no evidence to inform clinical decision-making. Finally, the study evaluates Everolimus monotherapy, which does not address the patient's specific multidisciplinary dilemma regarding the sequencing of PRRT and surgery (cytoreduction) following a partial response.
evaluation_results.trial_title: Phase IV Study of the Safety and Efficacy of Everolimus in Adult Patients With Progressive pNET in China

evaluation_results.explanation: This study does not provide meaningful evidence for this patient primarily due to a lack of biological alignment and treatment applicability. The patient has a well-differentiated Ileal (midgut) NET, whereas the SEQTOR trial is exclusively focused on Pancreatic NETs (pNET). This distinction is clinically critical because Streptozotocin-based chemotherapy (a core intervention in this study) is a standard treatment for pNETs but is generally not indicated or effective for midgut NETs. Consequently, the study's comparison of chemotherapy versus everolimus sequencing cannot be extrapolated to the patient's care. Furthermore, the input data indicates no published results are available, meaning there is no evidence to assess. Finally, the study does not address the patient's specific clinical question regarding the sequencing of PRRT and surgery.
evaluation_results.trial_title: Sequentiality of Everolimus and STZ-5FU in Advanced Pancreatic Neuroendocrine Tumor
